newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa vaults trend line, faces resistance.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa vaults trend line, faces resistance.

text.p: London cocoa futures sprang out of a rigid downtrend on Wednesday on the back of a New York rally but the move lacked vigour and soon met technical resistance. Buyers were sparse as March cocoa bounced to a session high of 927 stg and commission houses and speculators quickly jumped in to take profits, traders said.
But at midsession, the benchmark position crawled back from a low of 917 up to 925 stg a tonne, a 12 stg gain on the day, with the market volume totalling a modest 2,319 lots.
"There are specs looking to build positions under 900 on March, but as soon as they see reasonable profits they'll take it," said one trader.

Traders said London would be looking for clues from New York, where follow-up speculative and trade buying could suggest a trend change if the March contract secured its position above the sensitive $1,390 level.
In London, the 14-day RSI has cleared out of the oversold territory but stochastics are not yet signalling a change in pattern, analysts said.

Sterling's renewed strength continued to stifle business in the physical cocoa market. Cocoa continued to arrive in Amsterdam but tonnages were not great. Differentials were weakening and many shippers preferred to stay out.
Traders were also disappointed by lack of buying interest from Germany where sterling gains against the mark made the industry uncompetitive.
Ivorian cocoa for January shipment was being offered at 20-25 stg under the London March futures contract while December was bought at 25 stg under, and was offered at 17.
